sections.text: Under my guidance, Nature produces all things movable and immovable. Thus it is, O Arjuna, that this universe revolves.
Fools disregard Me, seeing Me clad in human form. They know not that in My higher nature I am the Lord-God of all.
Their hopes are vain, their actions worthless, their knowledge futile; they are without sense, deceitful, barbarous and godless.

We have been discussing chapter nine and what we have learned is that Bhagavan said, I am the source of all the things, all the beings, everything that you see. I am the source and I am also the final resting place for all things. Things come out of me and they will return back into me.
There is nothing really that can exist without me. As we said in that classical example, a ghost cannot exist without the post. So from the posts point of view, the post can say the ghost came out of me.
And once you realize there is no ghost, it also goes back into me. At any given time the ghost has no modifications or it never changed into ghost. But my ignorance and my perception has created this perception of a ghost.
In a similar way, Bhagavan says from me the whole Prakriti comes into existence. This world of plurality as you see, is because of my existence. If Im not there, there is no world of plurality.
This world as we know is I. And the world only exists because the fundamental basic reality is the self. I know I exist because of myself.
You know you exist because of yourself. She knows she exists because of herself. But we think these are different selves.
Bhagavan says its just me, myself reflecting through all of them. But we dont recognize it because of Mogha Asha -- vain desires. I think I am the center of my universe.
The world needs to revolve around my desires. I want things to be like this, I want the world to be like this, I want the market to do this when I invest. And therefore we do the wrong actions.
Because I have now considered this limited being as me, I now have my false desires. We know we have very little power over how things work in this world. But when we act, we forget what we know.
Even buying a gallon of milk -- so many people do so many things to bring that gallon of milk to your nearest Martins or Food Lion. Then, and only then, can you go and buy it. But I think that if I have $4 in my pocket, Im the king and can buy that milk.
That Mogha Asha creates this false notion that I am in control. And Bhagavan says Mogha Jnana Vichetasaha -- because of this false knowledge that this is me and I can change this world as I want, we create a false notion of control. Rakshasim Asuram Chaiva -- these people are of the nature of Rakshasa and Asura.
Rakshasa is one who is predominated by the Rajasic nature. We have seen in Vedanta that nothing can exist in this world of time and space if it does not have these three qualities of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas -- the fundamental classifications of the basic gunas. For any effect to exist in time and space, you need Sattva, which is the awareness that this exists.
Then there is the activity -- the intense activity we see at the atomic level, subatomic level, or even at the level of our daily experience. And then Tamas, the inertia for the thing to remain in its state as long as it can, until another force changes it. He said that those with the most Rajasic predominance are the Rakshasas, because they consider that their activity will give them control over their world.
And the Asuras are the Tamasic ones, with the predominant quality of Tamas. They rely on inertia. If I dont do anything, things wont change.
Lets keep things as is, dont change it. Not realizing that the nature of this world is Samsara -- constantly changing. In that Samsara, I try to keep things inert, as is.
That is the nature of the Asura. These two qualities make us forget the real nature of the self. In contrast to that -- Mahatmanastumam Partha, Devim Prakritim Ashritaha.
There is another group of people who do not fall into these two categories of Rajasic and Tamasic. The Rajasic and Tamasic are constantly interested only in material existence. They see their physical existence and say, My goal in life is to maintain this existence and have as much pleasure from this world as possible -- not realizing that this is a temporary existence in time and space.
But my real existence is infinite, permanent, immutable -- in the nature of the self. The other group of people, the Mahatmas, are great souls simply because they realize the nature of the self. Mahatmanastumam Partha, Devim Prakritim Ashritaha -- because they have taken refuge in the divine nature of the self, which is to recognize Sattva, the truth, that eternal truth which does not change with time.
Everything in this world is relative truth. Somebody says, What is it? I say, Its a day outside. Well, thats a relative truth. It was not true at 4 oclock in the morning.
It will not be true at 8 oclock at night. It is true only now in this time. So its called a relative truth.
But the truth which remains constant in any period of time is called Sattva, which I can say it was this 150 years ago. It is now and it will be for eternity. Thats the universal truth, the Sattva.
Those who take taken refuge into this awareness of that immutable truth which is the nature of the self. My self is not this limited being which has started its life on day one time. When I was born and Ill die is time T2.
And I want to make the most out of this life. Between this span of T1 and T2 are those Asuras and Rakshasas. But one who says, This is just a flicker in my existence.
My existence was infinite before and will be infinite after. I want to achieve that sense back, not get bogged down with this limited being -- those are the great souls. They identify not with the limited self, but with the higher self.
Here is the example I have used many times, because Im an architect. The space in this room is a conditioned space. Right now my association with this space is room space conditioned by these walls, floor, and ceiling.
But I also recognize that this space is universal space. It is here and it will be here, whether this building is there or not. The one who recognizes that myself will always be here, whether his body is there, mind is there, or intellect is there or not.
They are the great souls. Therefore they have taken refuge in the Daivi Prakriti -- this Sattva, predominantly Sattvic in nature. They recognize the ultimate truth about their own self.
Bhajanti ananya manasaha. Therefore they devote themselves to me with a single-pointed mind. Now obviously there are word connotations that come from our own experience in life.
Bhajanti -- with that kirtan and all that, you know. Bhajanti ananya manasaha, satatam. So constantly they are doing this.
But thats not possible in the literal sense. But we know that the Vedantic connotation of the word bhajanti means love. Love for the Divine is devotion.
Love is nothing but identification. The more I identify with someone, the more my love increases. The more I identify with the Divine.
So ananya manasaha means without any other thought -- without any other thought that this limited being is me. Im not an architect, Im not a father, Im not a son. All these are superimpositions on me.
Amitabh Bachchan never forgets when he plays the coolie that he is Amitabh Bachchan. He never forgets while doing all these roles he plays. I too play all these roles, but I forget and get identified with them.
And I get carried away with them. The Mahatma never gets carried away. So bhajantim Ananya Manasaha Gnatva Bhut adim avyam.
Knowing that I am the source of all the beings imperishable. We typically see that the source get destroyed into you take a seed and seed becomes a tree. The seed is no more there.
Now I can say, okay, now I want the seed back. Thats a perishable source of the tree. Bhagavan said, but I am the source of this universe.
All the being but imperishable never get destroyed. Because the creation is a Maya Post never became ghost. Therefore it never had to go into any transformation into something else.
So once you see the ghost, post doesnt go away. It remains exactly what it was before. Bhagavan says, knowing that I am the immutable, imperishable source of all the beings.
These Mahatmas wants to get back to their original self. At the immutable, imperishable self. They drop the identification with the limited.
Playing this part very efficiently in this world. But always the identification is with the higher self. Just as Amitabh Bachchan never forgets in Amitabh Bachchan.
But he is a coolie at the time. You know, say, Satatam Kirtayantah maam Yatan taschadiravratah. So now what will be my attitude once I have recognized that this limited being is not me.
This life is just a part I am playing for the time being. Before I was born, I existed as the universal being. After that all existed as a universal being.
Before this building was built, this space was here. And I can vouch for it because I live here long enough. Long before this building was here, this space was here.
After the building is built, theres room spaces here. And someday somebody will decide we can do better use of this land. And the building will be gone, but the space will be here.
I am here, I was here and I will be here. Thats the eternal truth. Bhagavan says Satatam Kirtayantah.
Having known this, so what will be my actions? Satatam constantly Kirtayantaha. I am singing the glory of that eternal self that I am my Lord, who functions through me as this limited being. Kirtan du Visival.
We have a bhajan, you know, next week. So thats the kirtan. Thats the only time we do kirtan Bhajan and kirtan.
This singing, with equally crude and noisy instruments -- it has its own place, for that time only, to occupy the mind. Because at least at that time, my mind is focused on those songs and the verses and what they mean. At that time, Im not thinking of anything else.
Those who do any kind of art know this -- the mind has to be occupied with something. And if it doesnt occupy, then it wanders away. One whose mind is constantly attached to that understanding that I am not this limited self, this universal self is manifesting in this world.
There is nothing that can exist in this world without Him. And therefore there is no existence for anything else other than that. If God is all pervading, where are we? If we are here, then he is limited.
He cannot be all pervading. So if he is all pervading, there is no place for anyone else. All that I see is nothing but his manifestations.
So now that constantly when I see anything in this world, the thought at the back of my mind says, that is nothing but the Lords manifestation. Whether that is good, bad or ugly. See, we have no problem.
We see something very beautiful, nice, and divine -- Thats Gods manifestation. Early morning the sun rises and we see, O God! But when we see darkness and evil and still see his presence in it -- thats where the real test is. Then my Kirtan, Bhagavan says, is complete, no matter what I encounter. I know he pervades the entire universe and all its happenings.
Nothing other than him can exist, and therefore there cannot be anything other than Him.

Fools disregard Me, seeing Me clad in human form (avajnanti mam mudha manusim tanum asritam). The Divine pervades everything, yet we fail to recognize it because we expect something extraordinary. We look for God in temples and sacred texts while ignoring the consciousness that animates every being we meet. The Divine is not hiding - it is the most obvious reality, present in every eye that sees, every heart that beats. Our failure to perceive it comes from looking for the wrong thing in the wrong way.
Those caught in Mogasha (vain desires), Moghakarma (vain actions), and Moghajnana (vain knowledge) live as if they are the center of the universe, believing their limited efforts can secure lasting happiness. Dominated by Rajasic (restless activity) and Tamasic (inertia) tendencies, they remain blind to the Sattvic truth of their own divine nature. The Rakshasa nature says I will acquire and control, the Asura nature says I will resist all change - both miss the recognition that the Self is already complete.
Self-inquiry for this week: Examine your primary operating mode. Are you driven by endless activity toward acquisition (Rajasic)? Or by resistance and avoidance (Tamasic)? Neither brings lasting peace. The alternative is to cultivate Sattva - the quality of awareness that recognizes the Divine presence in all. Today, practice seeing the same consciousness looking out from every pair of eyes you encounter. What shifts when you recognize that the one perceiving through you is perceiving through all?
